p.src: Now the gentleman who had broken Qiao Daoqing’s sorcery within the Song ranks was none other than Gongsun Sheng, the Dragon in the Clouds. After receiving Vanguard Song’s orders at Weizhou, he had set out with Wang Ying, Zhang Qing, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao, traveling through the night to reach the army. He entered the camp and paid his respects to Vanguard Song just as Qiao Daoqing was displaying his sorcery and defeating Fan Rui. That day was the eighth of the second month; its cyclical designation was wuwu, and wu belonged to earth. Gongsun Sheng therefore summoned the divine general of the heavenly stem, overcame the ren-gui waters, swept away the sorcerous miasma, and restored the clear blue sky and bright sun. Song Jiang and Gongsun Sheng rode together to the front and saw Qiao Daoqing, his face covered with shame, leading his troops away to the south. Gongsun Sheng said to Song Jiang, “Qiao Daoqing’s magic has failed and he is fleeing. If we let him enter the city, he will become firmly entrenched. Brother, quickly give orders for Xu Ning and Suo Chao to lead five thousand men around from the eastern road to the south gate and cut off his retreat. Have Wang Ying and Sun Xin lead five thousand men at full speed to block the west gate. If Qiao Daoqing arrives there in defeat, they need only bar his way into the city and need not engage him in battle.” Song Jiang issued orders according to this plan, assigning the commanders their several tasks, and they departed in obedience.

p.src: It was still around the hour of the Snake. Song Jiang and Gongsun Sheng led seven chiefs—Lin Chong, Zhang Qing, Tang Long, Li Yun, Hu Sanniang, and Gu Dasao among them—and twenty thousand troops in a murderous pursuit. The northern commanders, Lei Zhen and the others, protected Qiao Daoqing as they fought and retreated. More troops approached from ahead: Sun Qi and Nie Xin had led men to their aid, and the two forces joined. They had just reached the stronghold on Mount Wulong when they heard the Song troops behind them sounding gongs and beating drums, their battle cries shaking the heavens as they raced in pursuit. Sun Qi said, “Let the Imperial Preceptor enter the stronghold and establish his position. We shall fight them to the death.” Qiao Daoqing had boasted before all his commanders, and until now he had never met an equal in magic. Being so closely pressed by the Song troops filled him with shame and fury, and he said to Sun Qi, “You men withdraw for now. I shall go forward and meet the enemy.” He at once reined in the troops and arrayed them for battle, placing himself foremost while Lei Zhen and the other commanders clustered around him. Qiao Daoqing shouted, “How dare you bandits from the marsh bully a man so outrageously! I shall contest victory and defeat with you once more.” Qiao Daoqing had been born and raised in Jingyuan, in the far northwest, a great distance from Shandong, and so knew little about Song Jiang and his sworn brothers.

p.src: The banners in the Song formation now swept left and right, rising and falling as the troops formed their battle array. With the two armies facing each other, horns blared and war drums thundered together. In the southern formation the yellow standard moved; the gate banners parted, and two riders emerged. The central rider was Song Gongming of Shandong, known as the Protector of Justice and Timely Rain; on the horse to his left sat Gongsun Yiqing, the Dragon in the Clouds. Sword in hand, he pointed at Qiao Daoqing and said, “What you have learned is all heretical trickery, untouched by the true Way. Dismount and submit at once!” When Qiao Daoqing looked closely, he saw that this was indeed the gentleman who had broken his magic. Behold him: jade clustered upon his starry crown, gold threaded through his crane-feather robe. His Nine Palaces robe shone like rosy clouds; his treasured formulas concealed the wind and thunder of the Six Jia. A many-colored silken cord encircled his waist; in his hand he bore an ancient pine-grained sword. He wore a pair of scarlet cloud-stitched court shoes and rode a proud, high-headed horse with a yellow mane. His divine brows spread like the character eight above almond-shaped eyes, and a full beard covered his mouth and fell along his cheeks.

p.src: Qiao Daoqing now said to Gongsun Sheng, “My magic merely happened to fail today. Why should I submit to you?” Gongsun Sheng said, “Do you still dare show off that damned trickery?” Qiao Daoqing shouted, “You underestimate me! Watch my magic once more!” Qiao Daoqing gathered his spirit, muttered an incantation, and beckoned toward Fei Zhen. The tempered-steel spear in Fei Zhen’s hand suddenly flew from his grasp as though snatched away, rose like a soaring serpent, and thrust at Gongsun Sheng. Gongsun Sheng pointed his sword toward Qin Ming. The wolf-toothed mace had already left Qin Ming’s hand and flew to meet the steel spear; back and forth they battled in the air as swiftly as the wind. Both armies cheered again and again. Suddenly there came a tremendous crash, and both armies cried out. The wolf-toothed mace struck the spear from the sky; with a thud it plunged point-first into the northern army’s war drum and pierced it through. The soldier responsible for the drum turned ashen with fright. The wolf-toothed mace returned to Qin Ming’s hand just as before, as though it had never left it, and the Song troops laughed until their eyes narrowed to slits. Gongsun Sheng shouted, “You are showing off your axe before a master carpenter!” Qiao Daoqing again formed a hand seal and chanted a spell. Beckoning northward, he cried, “Come at once!” Behind the northern encampment, a mass of black cloud suddenly rose from a hollow on Mount Wulong. A black dragon appeared within it, spreading its scales and bristling its mane as it flew forward. Gongsun Sheng laughed heartily and likewise beckoned toward Mount Wulong. From a hollow in the mountain a yellow dragon shot out like lightning, half veiled in cloud and half in mist. It met the black dragon and fought it in the air. Qiao Daoqing called again, “Azure Dragon, come quickly!” An azure dragon had only just flown from the mountaintop when a white dragon followed it out, rushed forward, and intercepted it. The soldiers of both armies stared in stunned amazement. Brandishing his sword, Qiao Daoqing shouted, “Red Dragon, come quickly to our aid!” In a moment, a red dragon rose from the hollow and came flying and wheeling forward. The five dragons whirled wildly through the air, corresponding precisely to the five phases of metal, wood, water, fire, and earth. Generating and overcoming one another, they tangled into a single mass. A violent gale arose. In the two formations, the standard-bearers were caught by the wind, and scores of them were overturned one after another. Gongsun Sheng held his sword in his left hand and tossed his horsetail whisk skyward with his right. It rolled over in the air and turned into a bird like a wild goose, which flew upward. In moments it climbed higher and grew larger, soaring straight into the ninth heaven, where it became a great roc whose wings were like clouds hanging from the sky, and plunged upon the five dragons. A rending crash sounded like a thunderbolt in a clear sky, and the five dragons were battered until their scales and armor flew apart. Mount Wulong was in fact a numinous place where clouds of five colors often appeared. The dragon god had appeared to local people in dreams, and so they had built a temple with a spirit tablet to the Dragon King enshrined at its center. Following the five directions, they had also fashioned azure, yellow, red, black, and white dragons, each coiled around a pillar in its proper quarter. All were molded from clay, gilded, and brightly painted. The two men’s magic had now summoned these dragons to battle. Gongsun Sheng transformed his horsetail whisk into a great roc, which smashed the five clay dragons to powder and sent the fragments showering down chaotically upon the northern troops. The northern troops cried out and could not dodge fast enough. The old, sun-hardened clods of clay split faces and pierced foreheads, sending fresh blood spurting. More than two hundred men were injured on the spot, and the army scattered in confusion. Qiao Daoqing was helpless and had no spell to undo what had happened. The yellow clay tail of a dragon fell from the sky and struck him squarely on the head, nearly cracking his skull and crushing his Daoist crown flat. Gongsun Sheng beckoned with his hand. The great roc vanished without a sound, and the horsetail whisk returned to his grasp.

p.src: When Qiao Daoqing tried once more to work his sorcery, Gongsun Sheng invoked the divine power of the Orthodox Five-Thunder Rite. Above his head appeared a golden-armored deity, who thundered, “Qiao Lie, dismount and submit to arrest!” Qiao Daoqing muttered incantations under his breath, but they had not the slightest effect. Thrown into such a panic that he knew not what to do, he whipped his horse around and fled toward his own lines. Lin Chong spurred after him with spear in hand, shouting, “You sorcerous Taoist, stay where you are!” From the northern ranks, Ni Lin galloped out with sword raised and intercepted him. Lei Zhen charged forward with his halberd to assist him, while Tang Long galloped out from this side and blocked him with his iron melon hammer. Both armies raised wave after wave of battle cries as the four officers fought in two pairs before the lines. Ni Lin and Lin Chong fought for more than twenty bouts without either gaining the advantage. Lin Chong spotted an opening and thrust his spear into the horse’s leg. The animal fell, pitching Ni Lin to the ground, where Lin Chong drove a spear straight into his heart and killed him. Lei Zhen was locked in fierce combat with Tang Long when he saw Ni Lin fall. Feigning an opening, he wheeled his horse to flee, but Tang Long overtook him and brought the iron melon hammer down upon the crown of his head, smashing helmet and skull together and killing him beneath his horse. Song Jiang pointed with the tip of his whip, and Zhang Qing, Li Yun, Hu Sanniang, and Gu Dasao all charged forward together. The northern army fell into chaos and scattered in every direction to save their lives; great numbers were slain.

p.src: Sun Qi, Nie Xin, Fei Zhen, and Xue Can guarded Qiao Daoqing as they abandoned the stronghold on Five-Dragon Mountain and led their troops toward Zhaode. After rounding a hillside, while still six or seven li from the city, they suddenly heard war drums thunder ahead and mighty battle cries arise. A force burst from a narrow road to the east, led by two commanders: Xu Ning, the Golden Lancer, and Suo Chao, the Impetuous Vanguard. Before the two armies could engage, the defenders of Zhaode saw the fighting outside the walls. The garrison commanders Dai Mei and Weng Kui led five thousand men out through the south gate to provide support, and Xu Ning and Suo Chao split up to meet the enemy. Suo Chao detached two thousand troops to resist them from the north. Dai Mei took the lead and fought Suo Chao for more than ten bouts, until Suo Chao swung his gold-dipped axe and hewed him in two. Weng Kui hurriedly led his troops back into the city. Suo Chao pursued and slew more than a hundred northern soldiers, chasing them all the way to the south gate, but Weng Kui’s troops had already entered the city. They hastily raised the drawbridge and barred the gates. Logs and stone shot rained down from the walls, forcing Suo Chao to withdraw his troops.

p.src: Meanwhile, Xu Ning led three thousand troops to block the northern army’s path. Though the northern army had suffered one defeat, it still numbered more than twenty thousand men. The two commanders Sun Qi and Nie Xin engaged Xu Ning’s forces. Fei Zhen and Xue Can had no heart to prolong the battle. Leading five thousand troops, they guarded Qiao Daoqing as they fled westward. Xu Ning fought Sun Qi and Nie Xin with all his strength, but the northern troops closed around him. Hopelessly outnumbered, he was soon nearly trapped at the very center of the encirclement. Just then, the forces of Suo Chao and Song Jiang arrived from north and south. Unable to withstand an attack from three sides, Sun Qi and Nie Xin faltered. Xu Ning struck Nie Xin’s left arm with his golden spear, knocking him from his horse, and men and horses trampled him into pulp. Sun Qi forced open a path and tried to escape, but Zhang Qing overtook him and, with a single thrust, drove his spear into his back and knocked him from the saddle. The northern army was utterly routed, and more than half of its thirty thousand troops were slain. Corpses covered the fields and blood flowed in rivers. Countless gongs, drums, banners, armor, and horses were abandoned, while the surviving troops scattered and fled.

p.src: Song Jiang, Gongsun Sheng, Lin Chong, Zhang Qing, Tang Long, Li Yun, Hu Sanniang, and Gu Dasao joined forces with Xu Ning and Suo Chao, bringing their total strength to twenty-five thousand. Hearing that Qiao Daoqing had fled west with Fei Zhen, Xue Can, and five thousand troops, they wished to pursue him. By then it was the hour of the Monkey. The troops had fought bitterly all day and were hungry and exhausted. Vanguard Song was about to withdraw to camp for food and rest when a messenger arrived. Strategist Wu Yong, knowing that the vanguard and his troops had fought for many hours, had specially ordered Fan Rui, Shan Tinggui, and Wei Dingguo to muster ten thousand men, prepare torches, and come to their support. Vanguard Song was delighted. Gongsun Sheng said, “Now that we have this force, Elder Brother may return to camp with the other chieftains for food and rest. I shall take Chieftains Fan, Shan, and Wei and lead the troops in pursuit of Qiao Daoqing. We must make that fellow submit.” Song Jiang said, “It was through your miraculous powers, worthy brother, that we were delivered from disaster. You have come a long way and are weary from the journey. Return to the main camp with us and rest; we can deal with the matter again tomorrow. That fellow Qiao Daoqing has had his magic broken and exhausted all his stratagems. Surely there is nothing more to fear from him.” Gongsun Sheng replied, “There is something Elder Brother does not know. My master, the Immortal Luo, often told me: ‘There is a man in Jingyuan named Qiao Lie. He possesses the makings of a Taoist adept and once came seeking the Way, but I refused him for the time being, because his demonic heart was still too strong. The creatures of the mortal world were likewise generating evil, and the destined season of killing had not yet ended. Later, his demonic heart will gradually recede. When the destined opportunity arrives, he will encounter Virtue and submit. As fate would have it, he will encounter you. You may enlighten and convert him, and afterward he too will awaken to the mysteries of the Way. There will also come a time when he can be of use.’ While I was in Weizhou, I obeyed his command and came here. On the way I inquired into the sorcerer’s origins. General Zhang said that the surrendered officer Geng Gong knew all the particulars and had reported that Qiao Daoqing was none other than Qiao Lie of Jing County. When I saw his magic just now, I found his powers nearly equal to my own. But my master, the Immortal Luo, taught me the Orthodox Five-Thunder Rite, and that is why I was able to break his spells. This city is called Zhaode, which accords with my master’s prophetic words: ‘Encountering Virtue, the demon shall submit.’ If we allow him to escape and he should fall back into demonic delusion, we would be violating my master’s decree. We must not miss this opportunity. I shall lead the troops in pursuit at once and find the proper occasion to make him submit.” These words opened Song Jiang’s mind completely, and he thanked Gongsun Sheng again and again. He then led the other commanders and their troops back to camp for food and rest. Gongsun Sheng, together with Fan Rui, Shan Tinggui, and Wei Dingguo, led ten thousand troops in pursuit of Qiao Daoqing; of this, no more for now.

We must not miss this opportunity. I shall lead the troops in pursuit at once and find the proper occasion to make him submit.”
These words opened Song Jiang’s mind completely, and he thanked Gongsun Sheng again and again.
He then led the other commanders and their troops back to camp for food and rest.
Gongsun Sheng, together with Fan Rui, Shan Tinggui, and Wei Dingguo, led ten thousand troops in pursuit of Qiao Daoqing; of this, no more for now.

p.src: Meanwhile, Qiao Daoqing, Fei Zhen, and Xue Can led five thousand battered remnants in flight to the west of Zhaode. They were about to enter by the west gate when drums and horns suddenly sounded together. A force swept out from behind the dense woods ahead, led by two commanders: Wang Ying, the Stumpy Tiger, and Sun Xin, the Little Yuchi. With five thousand troops they deployed for battle and blocked the road. Fei Zhen and Xue Can fought desperately to break through. Obeying Gongsun Yiqing’s order, Sun Xin and Wang Ying merely prevented them from entering the city and did not pursue or slaughter them, but allowed them to flee northward. Those in the city knew that Qiao Daoqing’s magic had failed, that his forces had suffered a crushing defeat, and that Song Jiang’s army was overwhelmingly strong. Fearing the city might be lost, they kept the gates tightly shut and dared not come out to support him.

p.src: Before long, Sun Xin and Wang Ying saw Gongsun Sheng approaching at great speed with Fan Rui, Shan Tinggui, and Wei Dingguo at the head of their troops. Gongsun Sheng said, “You two chieftains should return to the main camp and rest. This humble Daoist will pursue him alone.” Sun Xin and Wang Ying obeyed his order and returned to camp. By then it was already around the hour of the Rooster. Meanwhile, Qiao Daoqing, together with Fei Zhen and Xue Can, led the shattered remnants northward, frantic as homeless dogs and desperate as fish escaped from the net. Gongsun Sheng, with Fan Rui, Shan Tinggui, and Wei Dingguo, led ten thousand troops in close pursuit. Gongsun Sheng shouted, “Qiao Daoqing, dismount and surrender at once! Persist no longer in your delusion!” From horseback ahead of them, Qiao Daoqing called back loudly, “Every man serves his own lord. Why must you press me so relentlessly?” Night had now fallen. The Song troops lit torches and brands, whose flames shone as brightly as broad daylight. Qiao Daoqing looked about him and saw only Fei Zhen, Xue Can, and some thirty horsemen; all the other men and mounts had scattered and fled. Qiao Daoqing tried to draw his sword and cut his own throat, but Fei Zhen hastily seized it and said, “Your Eminence must not do this.” Pointing with his hand toward a mountain ahead, he said, “We can hide in those hills.” At the end of his resources and strength, Qiao Daoqing rode into the hills with the two generals. Northeast of Zhaode stood Baigu Ridge, where, according to tradition, Shennong had tasted the hundred grains. Within the mountains stood a temple dedicated to Shennong. Qiao Daoqing and the two generals, Fei and Xue, established themselves in the Temple of Shennong, with only fifteen or sixteen horsemen remaining under their command. Gongsun Sheng allowed him to escape into the hills only because he wished to subdue and win him over. Otherwise, once the Song troops caught up, even ten thousand Qiao Daoqings would have been slain.

p.src: There is no need to dwell upon the matter. When Gongsun Sheng learned that Qiao Daoqing had fled into Baigu Ridge, he divided his forces into four columns, established camps, and surrounded the ridge on every side. Around the second watch, great flames suddenly appeared along the eastern and western approaches. It was because the Song vanguard, after returning to camp, had again ordered Lin Chong and Zhang Qing each to lead five thousand troops on an overnight reconnaissance, and they had now arrived. They joined forces with Gongsun Sheng, bringing their total strength to twenty thousand. They established separate camps and kept Qiao Daoqing under siege, of which no more need be said for now.

p.src: The next day, Song Jiang learned that Qiao Daoqing had been surrounded at Baigu Ridge by Gongsun Sheng and the others. He therefore consulted with Scholar Wu about taking the city. He ordered the main army to strike camp and advance to the walls of Zhaode. Song Jiang assigned his generals and officers their positions around Zhaode, sealing the city so tightly that not even water could leak through. Within the city, the defending commander Ye Sheng and the others held the walls tenaciously. The Song forces attacked for two days without cease, yet the city remained unbroken. In the camp south of the city, Song Jiang grew deeply distressed when he saw that the attacks had failed. Li Kui and the others had been trapped inside, and he did not know whether they were alive or dead. Before he realized it, tears streamed down his face. The strategist Wu Yong consoled him, saying, “Elder Brother, there is no need to grieve. A few sheets of paper are all we need to take this city with ease.” Song Jiang asked eagerly, “What excellent plan have you devised, Strategist?”

p.src: Scholar Wu calmly laid two fingers one over the other and revealed his plan—a plan destined to make the lone city fall without blood staining a blade, the soldiers cast aside their spears, and the people dwell in peace. But what did Scholar Wu say? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
